joe_customer: Hi — we've started seeing our Private control plane connections drop after a firewall update. App errors: 'tls: handshake failure (alert handshake_failure)'. ~10% of requests. Packet capture: https://uploads.example.com/captures/2245678901-custpcap.pcap

maria_support: Sorry for the pain — looking. Are you hitting private-control.redwood.example.com or a raw IP? Can you paste the exact failing log and time range?

joe_customer: Using private-control.redwood.example.com (CNAME -> cp-us-east-1.rw-inference.net). From our proxy logs: tls: received alert handshake_failure. tcpdump shows server sends Alert(HandshakeFailure). Only clients from our egress subnet 10.20.30.0/24 affected.

sam_oncall: Can you run: `openssl s_client -connect private-control.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private-control.redwood.example.com -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts` and paste output? Also a clienthello tcpdump would help. Does your egress NAT/proxy rewrite SNI?

joe_customer: Ran openssl; server aborts immediately. ClientHello in tcpdump shows SNI empty — our inline proxy strips SNI for certain destinations. tcpdump snippet: ```ClientHello SNI: ''``` We suspect the Palo FW rewrite pushed this change.

lee_neteng: That matches a pattern we saw: when SNI is missing, our control plane routes to a generic TLS listener that doesn't have the tenant-specific certs; the server then fails mTLS because the handshake lands on the wrong virtualhost. We pushed a change last week that tightened routing to require SNI.

maria_support: Ok — two remediation options: 1) Reconfigure your egress/proxy to preserve SNI (TLS passthrough). 2) We can stand up a temporary listener that accepts client certs without SNI (stopgap, requires eng-sre work). Which do you prefer for short term?

joe_customer: Vendor can't reconfigure until Monday. We need a quick fix — please enable the alternate IP path.

sam_oncall: Escalating. @eng-sre can you evaluate standing a temp listener that accepts no-SNI connections for this tenant? Need to verify no security regression.

eng-sre: We can create a temporary listener bound to a dedicated IP that accepts client certs without SNI, but we'll need: (a) the failing tcpdump, (b) your client cert chain (redacted), (c) list of egress IPs to permitlist. Also note: missing ALPN (h2/http/1.1) can also cause failures — check clienthello ALPN.

joe_customer: Uploaded pcap + openssl output + egress IPs 34.67.89.123, 34.67.89.124 here: https://uploads.example.com/captures/2245678901-custpcap.pcap

maria_support: Received. Opening internal ticket RW-INC-9412. Next steps for you: 1) confirm your egress allowlist includes our control-plane IP(s), 2) try the temporary IP once we provision it using: ```curl -v --resolve private-control.redwood.example.com:443:34.210.11.22 --cacert ca.pem --cert client.pem --key client.key https://private-control.redwood.example.com/status```

joe_customer: Ack — we'll test the temporary route and follow up. Vendor ETA for proxy fix is Monday. Thanks for the quick escalation.

dev-bot: Incident RW-INC-9412 created, priority P2, assignee eng-sre@redwood.com

sam_oncall: I'll monitor. Maria, please confirm timeline and when we add the IPs to the tenant's allowlist. Also recommend the customer add private-control domain to TLS passthrough exception on their proxy.

maria_support: Will do. Closing on this thread until eng-sre confirms temporary listener and we validate the workaround. :thumbsup:
